post_title: Hope this is ok to post this here, but what drink is this?
post_body: Hi went to costa for the first time in a while and ordered the peach ice tea, I've had it a good few times. The Barista called it a peach ice tea when she handed it to me. It's never looked like this when I've ordered this in the past and it's never been this red. It's usually orange-brown. It tastes different, not particularly sweet but not super bitter(I do have a high tolerance for bitter tho). I liked it so I asked the barista what it was and she was admin it was a peach ice tea and she just left the tea bag into long. It doesn't taste like supper strong tea and the colour is so red. Is this what happens when tea bag is left too long? Or did she accidentally make a different drink, if so any guess what it is? I really want to replicate the order cus it's good.

oh i’m gonna try that! and yeah i agree, i kind of like it for that though, kind of just a water with a hint of flavour
the thing is what throws me off is when you smell it you really get the mango coming through but the actual drink feels underwhelming in comparison to its scent?? like it’s lovely but underwhelming
I like an iced Earl grey with the mango sauce
haha yes tastes better imo too

post_title: How can I get a transfer to a Costa shop in a different city?
post_body:
Hi people. I will speak to my manager about this soon too, but just wondering what the process is for getting transferred to another store is? I'm likely going to move to another city in the new year and was hoping to just transfer to another Costa cafe so it would make the process of moving a lot easier as I would have a contract to show to get approved for renting a place and wouldn't have to deal with retail interviews which are mostly in-person and impossible for me to do in person until we move as it's 2 hours away.

Do I contact Costa shops in the city first and ask about a potential transfer, then connect them with my manager to organise it? I work in equity, so I assume equity to equity transfers are easy. Is equity to franchise also possible or would that process be more like applying for a brand new job, from a manager's point of view?

This will also be after Xmas so I'm aware of the chance that they don't need staff and can't authorise a transfer but I'd like to try anyway. Should I be contacting them with say 2 months notice or would contacting within 4 weeks of wanting a transfer be better, given how there's often people leaving and joining at random.

Hi there! I started working at Costa at the start of September (franchise), I only worked about 4 shifts before I had to leave due to some odd circumstances… I still haven’t received my pay for my work. Does anyone know why this would be? What days do franchise get paid? Thanks!

comments.body:
Franchise employees are paid for by the franchise partner. You didn’t work for Costa, you worked for the partner. You’ll be on their payroll and depending which franchise partner you work for, will dictate which day you should have been paid.

I’d suggest talking to your old store manager first and area manager second. If that isn’t successful, find out which franchise partner you worked for and contact their HR department.

Depends on which franchise you were. 
Scoffs group (the largest franchise)pay on the last working day of the month, which is tomorrow.

replies.body: For hourly paid employees?
For everyone.

comments.body: Check your employment documents to figure out when the payment date is. If you're paid monthly, you may still have to wait a bit more.

post_title: How likely are they going to invite you to interview if you have no barista experience
post_body: I am taking a year of uni (UK) so need a job. I scored high in the costa assessment but an pretty sure I am going to rejected pre interview based on how the job market is. Does anyone know how badly no barista experience will affect me?

comments.body: To be honest in our store we almost prefer no experience. Easier to train to our own brand standard with no pre-existing bad habits. And that isn't me saying that we are the best etc etc, but for things like Costa check it's just easier to be in good habits for the way we do things. So I wouldn't over-think it. Tbh we have just hired someone with hospitality experience and they're a nightmare because they think they know better about everything!

Really depends where abouts you are and whatever the local job market is like. If they need staff then they'll be more lax, but it's not the kind of job where there's a lot of transferable skills to put you above another candidate who does have barista experience. 


That being said, it is an entry level job so it shouldn't matter too much if you don't have experience. 


Tbh it really comes down to your area and how good or shite any given store management is

replies.body: Fingers crossed 🤞
Fingers crossed 🤞

comments.body:
i'm also in a gap year! costa makes coffee VERY differently to how a speciality coffee shop would make it. i'm new to costa, and all the staff at my costa have ONLY ever worked at costa, whereas my manager and i both have experience in other coffee shops. i was so surprised watching my coworkers make coffee... in costa, lattes are made backwards.. which REALLY confused me at first, but all my coworkers were a bit condescending and think that i'm dumb whenever i tell them how it's done outside of a costa.. so i think you are more than fine with no previous barista experience, and costa (other than the oddly condescending coffee talk lol) is a super nice environment to work in. i have a great manager who is a lot more chill when it comes to the costa rules.  
good luck !! you'll be fine
Depends how desperate they are for staff

it really depends. having no barista experience doesn't matter as much as you'd think. no matter what experience someone has, everyone has to go through the 6 week barista training. costa works on its own barista standard, which is hard to get the hang of if you're coming from another coffee shop. the only advantage baristas have is they'd understand the terminology better and will get a hang of making different milk textures faster, but they have old habits that costa doesn't appreciate so much. 

if you get an interview, make sure you show willing and express how much you enjoy customer service (we all know it's a lie, everyone i work with hates everything about customer service). my costa mostly hires baristas that have no experience. in the 10 months I've been there and the 6 other baristas that they've gotten through, I've been the only one with previous barista experience. if you're going for BM that's a different story, but then again, it's not unheard of having a BM with no barista experience

replies.body: Thank you, do they pay you during training?

yes, they do! they'll most likely have you on the computer for your first day doing the main online training and then after that you'll be on pots and till while having bits of coffee training in-between during quieter times, once you've completed your 6 week training you'll have free regin. coffee, bar, cold drinks, till, and pots. if you're progressing well during training, you might even be put on coffee with another barista. most of the time, though, the training takes a bit more than 6 weeks, I think mine took 3 months as I went on holiday in the middle of it.

my main advice would be to make sure you get your coffee measurements and grind&dose down straight away, make sure you memorise it, and take in every word your trainer tells you. you get tested at the end of each training module, and you need to pass it them all in order to become an actual barista. some trainers are very relaxed (mine was thankfully), but some may be stricter, so it's best to just try and retain everything you get told!

comments.body: When I worked at Costa most of the people we hired didn’t have barista experience

If you are applying now, they're probably looking to increase staffing leading up to Xmas. Even if your job is a permanent contract, the main thing is that this is the time where they tend to hire the most people in the year, so you probably have a better chance to get an interview than if you applied in January or February where there are fewer jobs going.

Heavily depends on the store though. Things that will affect your chance of being interviewed:

* Number of positions to be filled + number of total applicants

* Your availability (not sure if this is smth you state on your application though)

* Urgency of the job posting i.e. did one or more people just quit without notice

I got hired with some experience I could talk about on my CV (prior experience washing dishes in a smaller cafe) but I believe the main factor that got me  hired was that 1 or 2 people had quit suddenly, shortly before the manager was due to go on holiday. The manager also hired someone else alongside me who had 0 cafe experience and neither of us were temporary Xmas hires.

In summary I'd say from my experience applying many times before getting hired, no barista experience is a negative factor for the most part, but you could very well be invited for an interview with a high fit score if there are not too many applicants and at that point it's lowkey just a matter of learning how to answer the interview questions properly and also being likeable and coming across as someone they'd like to work with.
I was hired a couple of weeks ago with no previous barista experience

post_body:
Hi all, 

I'm entering the interview stage for a new drive thru opening near me and I've been told ahead of time that I will be getting 4 weeks of training at a drive thru about 30 minutes by bus (I've got no car). I'm entering this as a part time employee, making it clear that I only can do 12-16 hours a week. 

I was wondering if anyone had any similar experience to this? Obviously the training is paid right? But does my additional travel get expensed? As my training is at multiple different outlets from 1hr to 30 minutes away. How much training can I expect to do, considering I've never worked as a barista before? I'm a student so can't afford the time to dedicate more than 12-16 hours a week. Lastly, has anyone worked in a drivethru before? It doesn't sound as nice, considering there the new store will be drive thru only.

Of course these are all questions I'm going to ask in the interview but I wanted to get some answers ahead of time :)

comments.body: I work in a drive thru and personally prefer it to our normal ‘front till’ and seating area, we chat over the headsets and it’s just a lot easier to manage as only so many cars can fit in the queue so not as overwhelming
